- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak to avoid overshoot.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d), model often underestimates mean reversion; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize support; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to avoid undershoot.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment shifts or price stabilizes.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +0.3 and -0.1), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
